html:
The Saugeen complex was a First Nations culture on the southeast shore of Lake Huron and the Bruce Peninsula, in what is now Ontario, active from about 200 BCE to 500 CE. Its sites reach inland to the London area and possibly as far east as the Grand River.

Saugeen people fished, hunted and gathered, and made pottery. Like other Middle Woodland peoples of the region, they had some contact with the Hopewell trade world to the south. Their neighbours included the Couture people to the southwest, the Goodall people across Lake Huron in Michigan, and the Point Peninsula people to the east.

Archaeological evidence suggests that the Saugeen people of the Bruce Peninsula may have been ancestors of the Odawa, or Ottawa. The London area later became home of the Neutral confederacy.
